hypothesis: Canonical single-block unconditional zero-start/unit-step equality-exit loops with producer-local recurrences can use the existing bounded chunk schedule when full-trip scratch does not fit. Forwarding each retained PHI's exact original backedge seeds the next producer chunk without requiring original-loop vectorizability, a pressure/profitability threshold, a state array or wider control support. General examples are delayed loads, coupled state updates, ordered FP producer state and enclosing rows.
semantics: Retained PHIs now have a pre-mutation snapshot of Phi/Start/Backedge. Only the blanket retained-state chunk exclusion is removed; canonical control/polarity, finite count, representability, checked scratch/pointer indices, participation and effect proofs remain. Existing exact accumulator operand/use-edge closure is unchanged, so no moved reduction state can reach retained state, addresses, contributions or control. For each retained PHI the chunk header has a two-edge carry initialized from the original Start. Only its original preheader incoming block/value changes to the producer preheader/carry; its inner backedge and every producer operation/flag/order stay intact. A one-edge LCSSA PHI in the producer exit forwards the snapshot Backedge to the chunk latch -> chunk header edge. All forwards read the same final producer iteration, including older <- prev and prev <- state.next; no RAUW, updated-state substitution, arithmetic, freeze, reread or new poison consumption. Original ProducerExports separately forward current state, next state, contributions and indices on the final chunk exit. Original guards and zero-entry behavior remain. Existing LI construction, topmost SE invalidation, DT recalculation, stage metadata and recursive LCSSA checks remain. Strictfp/constrained FP/effects still reject. Unconstrained ordered FP retains every scalar operation and operand order; explicitly enabled fission FP reordering is a separate test policy with no fast-math/errno assumptions. Four focused exact-original fixtures and a separate original-order C oracle cover delayed loads, coupled integer state, ordered FP state and enclosing-row current/next-state feedback. Validation-only probes check exact incoming/final state at each chunk and complete producer-before-consumer execution with local scratch/global input indices. Counts and final exports make resetting state or using final current state as next seed fail. No executable checks have run in this worker.
costs: For R retained header PHIs, add R chunk-header carry PHIs and R single-edge producer-exit forwarding PHIs. Original retained PHIs remain; final producer exports are intentionally separate (7/8 in the new fixtures). Existing reduction carries/results stay unchanged (3 carries/results per new fixture). No retained-state arrays, scratch streams, masks, input rereads, duplicated producer operations, contribution recomputation or new runtime guards. The existing chunk min(N-base,C), ordinal counters and branches are reused. New fixtures share one i32 contribution across two reductions and one double contribution across the ordered FP reduction: C=1/9/16 reserves 16/112/192 bytes with ABI alignment; 15 bytes rejects even one slot. Logical stores are 12*N bytes and loads 12*N bytes per row (24*N total), zero on entry bypass; nested rows reuse the same entry allocations. Retained carry counts are 2/3/2/3 for delay/pair/FP/enclosing cases. Capacity binary search, finite-count/scratch/effect analysis and existing per-use closure do not change. Additional compiler work/storage is linear in header PHIs, without dependence walks, path enumeration, SSA reconstruction or a profitability model. Validation adds fixture-scoped instruction/edge certificates, bounded C state/oracle arrays, actual chunk/stage probes and linear completed-stdout accounting; validation-only input reads/computation are not generated compiler traffic. Physical stack use, spills, RVV traffic and speedup are unmeasured.
limitations: No builds, test runners, compiler invocations, host numerical comparisons or primary corpus compilations were run by this worker. Only source/diff/evidence review, Python AST parsing and whitespace inspection were performed. All new coverage is planned until the harness completes it. Chunk support still requires the existing canonical single-block unconditional zero-start/unit-step equality-exit schedule. No affine/relational, compact or multi-block retained-state chunking is added, and pending d2 work is not imported. This cannot establish SHTools coverage: both exact SHTools original targets reject scalar-unsupported-exit at the accepted base, and this task does not extend exit admission. The broad existing header-state type admission remains, but new numerical cases exercise i32/double state; pointer/other scalar carries and arbitrary poison inputs are not newly executed. Existing poison, feedback, effect and control regressions remain mandatory. Fixed-vscale host execution is not RVV target execution, and machine verification/code generation is not a speedup measurement.

Genuine feedback, unsafe-call, volatile, strictfp, constrained-FP, noncanonical and reverse-equality rejection checks remain, scoped per function instead of a global no-fission assertion.

At the dispatch 259-byte ceiling, interleave2/interleave3 now select C=64/B=256 with one retained XOR carry; their exported XOR and scalar updates are checked. The exact 260-byte full-trip expectations remain.

recurrence_over_capacity now selects C=5461/B=65536 for bound 5462, with four retained carries; the previous rejection existed solely because of the blanket retained-state exclusion. Its original IR is unchanged.

The historical recurrence_unbounded is also finite under its nonzero canonical equality control, as established by the unchanged SCEV/representability proof and the existing analogous scalar-ir-reject test. It now checks C=5461/B=65536 and four producer carries. Huge runtime counts remain IR/analysis-only coverage; no huge-count numerical execution is claimed.
